text:
mike: Quick RFC follow-up on precision gating. Proposal: add a 'quality_floor' tag to quant profiles so the runtime can auto-fallback when degscore > threshold. Want to capture tradeoffs and operational boundaries here.

sara: +1. Can you clarify where degscore is computed — client-side, model shim, or server-side?

mike: Server-side. Plan is to compute degscore from shadow evals + recent production shadow sampling and publish a per-profile score. Runtime consults cached score only, updates happen async.

dan: Main concern is latency/throughput. We shouldn't compute degscore on-path. Sliding-window async updates sounds good. How big is the window?

mike: Thinking 10k tokens aggregated over latest 1–3 hours by default. We keep token buckets per-profile; window size configurable per-customer.

alec: Another angle: per-sequence vs per-token degradation. Some regressions happen late in sequence. Can we detect tail collapse?

sara: We can keep tokenwise summaries (mean logprob by percentile, tail-snr). Runtime would use a heuristic: if tail_degrade_pct > X then trigger fallback for that request.

dan: :thinking_face: For Dedicated customers who want to override quant profiles, how do we expose this? They may want to force a low-bit profile for cost reasons even if degscore high.

mike: Add metadata fields to profiles: "enforceable" (bool) and "quality_floor" (float). If enforceable=true, runtime must respect the profile unless quality_floor exceeded. If enforceable=false, the runtime emits an audit warning and can follow operator overrides. Default for Dedicated: enforceable=true.

sara: Need to be explicit about staleness: when we update degscore, there should be a TTL and a version field. Rollback plan if scores look noisy.

mike: Agreed. Proposal: score has (value, version, ttl, provenance). Runtime only triggers fallback if score.version matches model_version or is newer.

mike: Draft of the state transitions (pseudo):
```
COLD -> (enough samples) -> WARM
WARM -> (sustained high degscore) -> FROZEN -> trigger fallback
FROZEN -> (manual/automated reset) -> WARM
```

alec: For long-context models, fallback might require switching to a different KV-cache format. Need contract on migratability between profiles.

mike: We'll require a compatibility matrix in the profile metadata: compatible_profile_ids: [...]. Runtime will fallback only to first compatible profile that meets quality_floor.

dan: Ops checklist: canary watch, alert thresholds, and a safe rollback route if we see mass fallbacks. Also, don't forget cost accounting changes.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Created canary job `quant-deg-monitor` in staging; schedule: every 5m sampling job.

mike: Next actions: I will write an RFC appendix with the state machine, API changes to /profiles (new fields: quality_floor, enforceable, compatible_profile_ids, score_meta) and a brief ops playbook. Owners: @mike (runtime), @sara (telemetry/metrics), @dan (ops/canary).

sara: I'll add telemetry dashboards for tokenwise percentiles and the degscore sliding window.

dan: I'll wire the canary alerts and ensure billing tags included.

mike: Thanks — will ping when appendix is up for review. :thumbsup:
